There is still so much misplaced stigma surrounding mental health wellness. MindFest, put on by the Conifer Rotary Club, is attempting to change that. This is a free mental wellness and health fair on February 17th at Our Lady of the Pines. 

More info ⬇️

Head Start offers education, health, and nutrition services to children from at-risk backgrounds.

Cuts to this program would directly impact 12,000 Children across CO. I led a letter with my colleagues in calling for increased funding for this program.⬇️

https://t.co/dADrmMRiSi https://t.co/q6nH3IKEny

Small businesses are the backbone of our local economies and we need to come together with bipartisan solutions to improve access to workforce housing, reliable internet, legal pathways for people to work, childcare, and access to mental health care and SUD treatment. (2/2) https://t.co/sO8WXg4WkY
It’s no surprise that the Republicans tried to offer an amendment to defund IVF treatment. We know they will not stop at abortion and will continue to strip our freedoms away across the country.

Rosa is a brave Coloradan facing a terminal cancer diagnosis who has always wanted to be a police officer. After her husband Aaron reached out to my team, we put them in touch with @LakewoodPDCO & made her dreams come true. Last week she was sworn in as an honorary officer!

Recovery is possible if we give people the care they need, my mom is proof of that. 

We just celebrated her 7-year anniversary in recovery after a decades long struggle with opioids. I've seen how hard it is to get coverage for treatment. That's why I introduced the Recovery Act https://t.co/I7HRXGBWAF

My mom wouldn’t be alive today without finally getting the treatment she needed, but I know she's one of the lucky ones.

Far too many people are left without care because of the stigma associated with addiction and the lack of funding. (3/4) https://t.co/SCdUGNw9Wo

When we give people access to the care they need, we give them a chance to live in recovery. My mom is proof of that. The Recovery Act, will expand access to treatment for substance use disorders, & help people who are often left behind enter into recovery.https://t.co/9QMZpRO9yv

In my fight to save my mom’s life from an opioid addiction, I saw firsthand how broken our system was & the lack of access to care. 

The Recovery Act will expand coverage, remove treatment limitations, & ensure evidence based care to save lives & address the opioid epidemic. https://t.co/Mppk6fdMAE

On this International Recovery Day, we honor the 21 million Americans living in recovery & recognize their resilience and strength, often made possible by access to evidence-based treatment. https://t.co/APy16IeIlv

The biggest barrier to treatment is the stigma surrounding addiction. 

We must share the stories of our loved ones to show what’s possible when people get the help they need. For me, that person is my mom.

I sponsored the referred measure that voters passed to establish the HSMA program in Colorado and will keep working to support federal funding for school nutrition programs so no child goes hungry in school. (2/2) https://t.co/EEAhT3XPbz

A 10 year old who was on her way to the doctor for brain cancer treatment was detained in Houston, alongside her 4 siblings, who are also US citizens, and her parents who are undocumented and have no criminal history. 

The entire family was deported to Mexico. This family’s story is heartbreaking and an example of what’s happening across the country with Trump’s atrocious immigration policies.

The GOP plan to slash Medicaid won’t just cost lives — it will also cut thousands of jobs in CO.

Hospitals will be strained. Pregnant women, Kids, & seniors will go without the treatment they need to survive.

All to give more tax breaks to billionaires.
https://t.co/qVbEGXuOxc

Members of the LGBTQ community aren't asking for special treatment – they're asking for the basic human right to live with dignity, safety, and equality.

While Trump and the GOP work to roll back LGBTQ+ rights and target our transgender youth, I’m proud to join my colleagues in introducing the Equality Act, which will protect LGBTQ+ individuals from discrimination in employment, housing, and all areas of public life.

Every person should be treated with the respect they deserve, regardless of who they are or who they love.

This is Athena. She struggled with her mental health and couldn’t afford the care she needed. Medicaid helped her get treatment so she could return to work. Now she helps others do the same.

Athena’s story reminds us all what’s at stake with the Republican budget cuts that will rip health care away from people like Athena.

This is Sunny from Wheat Ridge. After losing everything in a house fire, she relied on Medicaid and SNAP to support her family. Medicaid made sure her husband got epilepsy treatment and her son received care through Colorado’s autism waiver.

Republicans are pushing legislation that would rip that support away from moms and families like Sunny’s. I’m fighting to protect Medicaid—because no family should be left behind when they need help the most.

One of the most important parts of my job is hearing from everyone across my district.

It was so great to be in Fremont County recently to share more about my work in Congress to protect access to Medicaid, defend our public lands, and support the issues that matter most to Southern Colorado.

I’m thankful for the chance to hear directly from you and bring your voices with me to Washington.

🚨 Planned Parenthood just announced that they can no longer serve patients in Colorado who are covered by Medicaid because of the Republican’s disastrous budget bill that was just signed into law. 

These restrictions are horrific and cruel for the people who rely on public-funded support and need help the most. 

Like thousands of other women, I have also relied on Planned Parenthood for basic care when I couldn’t afford health insurance, and I’m devastated thinking about the women who will be left with nowhere else to go. 
https://t.co/UeDlC3s22M

Thank you to everyone who joined our town halls in Cañon City and Woodland Park - it means so much to hear directly from you. I know many Coloradans are scared — about losing access to care and about what comes next. 

One woman shared how Medicaid keeps her husband alive. Farmers told us how critical the program is to them. These stories stay with me. 

I want you to know: I will always show up for you.

Trump's Big Bad Bill is a catastrophe for our families

Hospitals and nursing homes will shutter. Kids will go hungry. ERs will be completely overrun. And our healthcare costs will skyrocket.

Trump said he was going to lower costs on day one. Instead he's wreaking havoc -- raising costs and pulling the rug out from families, kids, seniors and the disabled while dismantling the systems we all rely on.

60 years ago, America made a promise: we will not leave our seniors, people with disabilities and those living in poverty without the essential healthcare they need. Medicare and Medicaid have saved countless lives and lifted millions from poverty. Unfortunately today, that promise is under threat. 

We aren’t going to sit back while Republicans mislead the public about the bill they just passed and the detrimental impact to all of us, especially our seniors who are on a fixed income.

No more secrets. No more special treatment. No more waiting. No more.

The American people deserve the truth about every single person who participated in Epstein’s abuse @MeidasTouch 
https://t.co/n51eryeavL

I'm joining my CO Democratic colleagues in calling on @CMSGov to renew Colorado’s Medicaid waiver program to ensure our youngest kids will have continuous medical care and won’t be thrown into a system that is designed to kick them and their family members off.

This continuity of care prevents our kids from slipping through the cracks and is an essential investment in the lives of those who need our support the most.
